name: Allianz Travel Insurance
price_summary: Quote-based — premiums vary by trip cost, traveler age, dates, and state (no fixed list price; as of 2026-07-18). Single-trip OneTrip plans plus AllTrips annual plans.
pros: The Cancel Anytime upgrade has the highest published reimbursement of any provider we compared — it "can reimburse 80% of your lost non-refundable trip costs" for almost any unforeseeable reason, and lets you cancel up until the day of scheduled departure (per Allianz's official Cancel Anytime pages, as of 2026-07-18)

Broad published plan menu: four single-trip OneTrip plans (Basic, Prime, Premier, Emergency Medical) and four AllTrips annual plans (Basic, Prime, Executive, Premier), so frequent travelers have a documented annual option
Every plan includes the 24-Hour Assistance Hotline — multilingual assistance reachable by phone or the free Allyz app, per Allianz's official assistance page
The Epidemic Coverage Endorsement adds covered epidemic-related reasons to select benefits on eligible plans — a documented differentiator most competitors don't publish
cons: Cancel Anytime is not offered in all states, is only available on OneTrip Prime and Premier, and requires insuring your full trip cost within 14 days of your first trip payment with a departure at least 30 days out — miss any condition and the headline 80% benefit doesn't apply
Pricing is entirely quote-based, so you cannot compare Allianz's real cost against competitors without entering trip and traveler details

Which underwriter stands behind your policy (BCS Insurance Company or Jefferson Insurance Company) depends on your state and plan, and benefit availability — including the Epidemic Coverage Endorsement and the 15-day free look — also varies by state
best_for: Travelers who want the strongest published Cancel For Any Reason-style option (80% reimbursement, cancellable through the day of departure) and a documented annual-plan lineup.
summary: Allianz pairs the highest published CFAR-style reimbursement we found — the 80% Cancel Anytime upgrade — with a broad documented menu of single-trip and annual plans and 24/7 multilingual assistance. The trade-offs: Cancel Anytime is state- and plan-restricted with strict purchase conditions, and quote-based pricing makes comparison shopping laborious.
verdict_summary: Allianz Travel Insurance is our top overall pick because its published flexibility terms lead this comparison. The optional Cancel Anytime upgrade states it can reimburse 80% of lost non-refundable trip costs — the highest percentage among the five providers we compared — and allows cancellation up until the day of scheduled departure, per Allianz's official pages as of 2026-07-18. Around that headline sit four documented OneTrip single-trip plans, four AllTrips annual plans, a 24-Hour Assistance Hotline with the Allyz app, and an Epidemic Coverage Endorsement on eligible plans. The honest trade-offs: Cancel Anytime is not offered in all states, applies only to OneTrip Prime and Premier, and requires insuring the full trip cost within 14 days of your first payment for a trip departing at least 30 days out; pricing is quote-based; and underwriter and benefits vary by state. This rating analyzes Allianz's published documentation — we have not filed claims with any provider here.

faq.question: How much does Allianz travel insurance cost?

faq.question: What is Allianz's Cancel Anytime upgrade?
faq.answer: Cancel Anytime is Allianz's Cancel For Any Reason-style optional upgrade to OneTrip Prime and Premier. Allianz's official pages state it can reimburse 80% of lost non-refundable trip costs if you cancel for almost any unforeseeable reason your plan doesn't already cover, and you can cancel up until the day of scheduled departure. Conditions apply: insure your full trip cost within 14 days of your first trip payment, depart at least 30 days after purchase, and it is not offered in all states (as of 2026-07-18).

faq.question: Can I get a refund if I change my mind about a policy?
faq.answer: Allianz publishes a free-look period: you get 15 days to review your plan and can cancel for a full refund within 15 days of purchase — depending on your state of residence — provided you haven't filed a claim or departed on your trip (as of 2026-07-18).

evidence_points.claim: Cancel Anytime can reimburse 80% of lost non-refundable trip costs for almost any unforeseeable reason not already covered; it requires insuring the full trip cost within 14 days of the first trip payment, a departure at least 30 days out, and is not offered in all states (as of 2026-07-18).
Every Allianz travel protection plan includes 24/7 access to a multilingual assistance team, reachable by phone or the free Allyz app.

name: Travel Guard (AIG)
price_summary: Quote-based — no published list or "starting at" price (as of 2026-07-18). Essential, Preferred, and Deluxe single-trip tiers plus Pack N' Go, Medevac, and an Annual plan.
pros: The widest documented add-on customization in this comparison: the Deluxe plan page lists optional bundles including a Pre-Existing Medical Condition Exclusion Waiver, Adventure Sports, Name Your Family®, Pet, Wedding, Quarantine, and Rental Vehicle Damage coverage (as of 2026-07-18)
Unusual documented plan variety beyond the three main tiers — Pack N' Go for last-minute, post-departure-only coverage and a Medevac Per Trip plan for evacuation-focused needs
All plans include access to a specialized 24/7 emergency travel assistance team, per the official plans page
A published 15-day look period lets you review the policy and cancel, and underwriters are named on-site with NAIC numbers
cons: Cancel For Any Reason reimbursement is "typically 50%" of trip cost per Travel Guard's own CFAR page — the lowest published CFAR percentage in this comparison — and must be bought within 15 days of your initial trip payment, with cancellation at least 48 hours before departure
The Annual Travel Insurance Plan is not currently available to Washington residents, coverage may not be available in all states, and identity-theft assistance excludes New York residents
No published pricing at all — not even a "starting at" figure — so any cost comparison requires a full personal quote
best_for: Travelers who want to tailor coverage with documented add-on bundles — adventure sports, pets, weddings, pre-existing-condition waiver — rather than accept a fixed package.
summary: Travel Guard's documented strength is customization: three main tiers plus niche plans and the longest list of published add-on bundles we found. Its published CFAR terms are the weakest of the group at typically 50% reimbursement, and nothing about pricing is published, so real costs require a quote.
verdict_summary: Travel Guard ranks second on the strength of its documented customization. No competitor here publishes a longer add-on menu: the Deluxe plan page lists a Pre-Existing Medical Condition Exclusion Waiver plus Adventure Sports, Name Your Family®, Pet, Wedding, Quarantine, and Rental Vehicle Damage options, and the lineup includes last-minute (Pack N' Go) and evacuation-focused (Medevac) plans alongside Essential, Preferred, Deluxe, and an Annual plan — all with 24/7 emergency assistance and a 15-day look period, per travelguard.com as of 2026-07-18. The honest trade-offs: its Cancel For Any Reason upgrade reimburses "typically 50%" — the lowest published percentage in this ranking — with a 15-day purchase window and a 48-hour pre-departure cancellation deadline; the Annual plan excludes Washington residents; and no pricing is published without a quote. We analyze Travel Guard's published documentation only; we have not filed claims. For tailored coverage, it is the standout.

faq.question: Who underwrites Travel Guard policies?

evidence_points.claim: Travel Guard's Cancel For Any Reason upgrade reimburses "typically 50%" of insured trip cost, must be purchased within 15 days of initial trip payment at the same time as the base plan, and requires cancelling at least two days before departure (as of 2026-07-18).

name: Seven Corners
price_summary: Quote-based — no published list price (as of 2026-07-18). Trip Protection Basic and Choice single-trip plans, plus an Annual Multi-Trip plan and separate travel-medical, cruise, and evacuation lines.
pros: 75% Cancel For Any Reason is available as an add-on to BOTH documented single-trip tiers (Trip Protection Basic and Choice) — you don't have to buy the top plan to get the highest CFAR percentage, unlike Travelex and World Nomads (as of 2026-07-18)
Also offers Interruption For Any Reason (IFAR) — a documented add-on none of the other four providers here advertise
24/7 urgent travel assistance comes from Seven Corners Assist, the company's in-house team, per the official site
Unusually broad documented catalog beyond trip protection: travel medical, USA-visitor, cruise, medical evacuation, and expat/nomad health lines
cons: New York and Washington residents cannot purchase the Trip Protection plans at all, CFAR is "not available to NY residents," and covered reasons vary by residence state — a hard availability wall, not just a variation

The Annual Multi-Trip plan is materially different from the single-trip plans: a different underwriter (Spinnaker Insurance Company vs. United States Fire Insurance Company), outsourced assistance (battleface Robin Assist instead of Seven Corners Assist), and a shorter 10-day free look versus 14 days

During our review the Trip Protection Elite product page returned a server error, so we could verify Elite only through Seven Corners' program-summary document — thin public documentation for a headline plan (as of 2026-07-18)
best_for: Travelers who want the highest published CFAR percentage (75%) without paying for a top-tier plan, or who need IFAR, cruise, or travel-medical options from one documented catalog.
summary: Seven Corners puts its best flexibility terms on its mid-market plans: 75% CFAR attaches to both Trip Protection Basic and Choice, and it's the only provider here advertising Interruption For Any Reason. The trade-offs are hard state exclusions (no NY/WA purchases) and an annual plan whose underwriter, assistance provider, and free look differ from the single-trip plans.
verdict_summary: Seven Corners ranks third because its published Cancel For Any Reason access is the most democratic in this comparison: the 75% CFAR add-on — matching the highest percentage any provider here publishes for a standard CFAR — attaches to both Trip Protection Basic and Trip Protection Choice, not just a premium tier, with a 20-day purchase window from your initial deposit, per sevencorners.com as of 2026-07-18. It is also the only provider in this ranking advertising Interruption For Any Reason, and its 24/7 assistance is in-house (Seven Corners Assist). The honest trade-offs: New York and Washington residents cannot buy these plans at all; the Annual Multi-Trip plan swaps to a different underwriter (Spinnaker), outsourced assistance, and a 10-day rather than 14-day free look; and the Elite plan's public page was erroring during our review. This analysis reflects published documentation, not claims experience. For mid-priced CFAR access, Seven Corners leads.

faq.question: What does Seven Corners' Cancel For Any Reason cover?
faq.answer: Per Seven Corners' official pages, the optional CFAR add-on pays 75% of your non-refundable insured trip cost if you cancel for any reason not otherwise covered. It must be purchased within 20 days of your initial trip deposit, you must cancel before departure, and it is subject to eligibility criteria — it is not available in all states and not available to New York residents (as of 2026-07-18).

faq.question: Can anyone buy Seven Corners trip protection?
faq.answer: No. The official plan pages state that New York and Washington residents cannot purchase the Trip Protection plans, and covered reasons vary by your state of residence. Florida, California, New Hampshire, and Virginia residents also have distinct terms on the annual plan (as of 2026-07-18).

faq.question: Is the annual plan the same product as the single-trip plans?
faq.answer: Materially, no. The single-trip Trip Protection plans are underwritten by United States Fire Insurance Company with in-house Seven Corners Assist and a 14-day free look; the Annual Multi-Trip plan is underwritten by Spinnaker Insurance Company with assistance from battleface Robin Assist and a 10-day free look (as of 2026-07-18). Read the plan documents for the one you're actually buying.

evidence_points.claim: Seven Corners' CFAR add-on pays 75% of trip cost for cancellations not otherwise covered, requires purchase within 20 days of initial trip deposit, is not available in all states, and is not available to NY residents; IFAR is also offered (as of 2026-07-18).
Trip Protection Basic and Choice are underwritten by United States Fire Insurance Company, carry a 14-day free look (15 for Missouri), and cannot be purchased by New York or Washington residents.

name: World Nomads
price_summary: Quote-based — no published list price (as of 2026-07-18). Standard, Explorer, and Epic single-trip plans plus an Annual Multi Trip plan.
pros: The only provider in this comparison whose official site documents that you can buy a plan while already traveling and buy more coverage mid-trip to extend it — a genuine structural difference for long-term travelers (as of 2026-07-18)
Documented adventure-activity coverage is unmatched here: over 250 activities on Standard, Explorer, and Annual plans, and over 340 on the Epic plan, per worldnomads.com
Cancel For Any Reason is available as an add-on at two levels — up to 50% (max $5,000) on Explorer and up to 75% (max $11,250) on Epic
24/7 multilingual emergency assistance is included, connecting travelers with medical treatment and transportation
cons: Key policy terms are not published: the free-look period's length "is dependent upon which state you live in" with no number given, and the CFAR purchase window (days from trip deposit) is not stated on the plan page — you must read your specific policy to know your own deadlines
CFAR is not available in New York, must be exercised at least 2 days before departure, and the better 75% level requires buying the top Epic plan
Coverage terms vary by jurisdiction and "not all insurance coverages are available in all jurisdictions," per the site's own disclaimer
best_for: Adventure and long-term travelers who need documented coverage for hundreds of activities and the ability to buy or extend a policy after departure.
summary: World Nomads is structurally different from the other providers here: its site documents buying and extending coverage mid-trip and covers 250–340+ adventure activities depending on plan. The trade-off is thinner published terms — no stated free-look length and no published CFAR purchase window — so more depends on reading your specific policy.
verdict_summary: World Nomads ranks fourth overall but first for a specific traveler: the adventurer already on the road. Its official US site documents two things no competitor in this ranking matches — you can buy a plan while already traveling and extend coverage mid-trip, and its plans list coverage for over 250 adventure activities (over 340 on Epic), as of 2026-07-18. CFAR comes in two documented levels: up to 50% (max $5,000) on Explorer and up to 75% (max $11,250) on Epic, cancellable until two days before departure, though not in New York. The honest trade-offs are transparency: the free look exists but its length is only described as state-dependent, the CFAR purchase window isn't stated on the plan page, and the site warns that coverages vary by jurisdiction. Policies are underwritten by United States Fire Insurance Company. This rating analyzes published documentation, not claims experience. For adventurous, open-ended travel, it is the documented standout.

pricing_table.notes: Ascending tiers; over 250 covered activities on Standard and Explorer, over 340 on Epic; CFAR add-on available on Explorer (up to 50%, max $5,000) and Epic (up to 75%, max $11,250), not available in New York.
Year-round multi-trip coverage with over 250 covered activities, per the official US travel insurance page.

faq.question: Can I buy World Nomads coverage after my trip has started?
faq.answer: Yes — this is World Nomads' documented differentiator. Its official site states you can buy a plan online anytime, from anywhere in the world, and if you're traveling and want to extend your trip you can buy more coverage to stay covered (as of 2026-07-18).

faq.question: What adventure activities does World Nomads cover?
faq.answer: Per worldnomads.com, the Standard, Explorer, and Annual Multi Trip plans list coverage for over 250 activities, and the Epic plan for over 340 (as of 2026-07-18). Check your specific plan's activity list — coverage terms vary by jurisdiction.

faq.question: Does World Nomads offer Cancel For Any Reason?
faq.answer: Yes, as an optional add-on at two levels: up to 50% of trip cost (max $5,000) on the Explorer plan and up to 75% (max $11,250) on the Epic plan. You must cancel at least 2 days before departure, and it is not available in New York. The purchase-window deadline isn't stated on the plan page, so confirm it in your policy documents before relying on it (as of 2026-07-18).

evidence_points.claim: World Nomads' US plans are Standard, Explorer, and Epic plus an Annual Multi Trip option; CFAR is an optional add-on at up to 50% (max $5,000) on Explorer and up to 75% (max $11,250) on Epic, requires cancelling at least 2 days before departure, and is not available in New York (as of 2026-07-18).

The site documents buying a plan while already traveling and extending coverage mid-trip; plans list over 250 covered activities (over 340 on Epic); the free-look period's length is state-dependent; policies are underwritten by United States Fire Insurance Company.

name: Travelex Insurance Services
price_summary: Quote-based — no published list price (as of 2026-07-18). Essential, Advantage, and Ultimate comprehensive tiers plus Travel Med Go and two flight-only plans.
pros: The longest published free-look period in this comparison: 21 days to review the policy and get a full refund if you haven't departed or filed a claim, per travelexinsurance.com (as of 2026-07-18)

A simple, clearly documented lineup — three comprehensive tiers (Essential, Advantage, Ultimate) plus a travel-medical plan and two flight-only plans — with unusually detailed published state-by-state notes
Cancel For Any Reason on the Ultimate plan reimburses up to 75% of insured trip costs (max $7,500), tying the highest standard percentage here
A single named underwriter — Zurich American Insurance Company (NAIC #16535) — rather than a state-dependent roster, which makes the paper behind the policy easier to check
cons: CFAR is heavily fenced: only on the top Ultimate tier, only for trips costing $10,000 or less, purchased within 21 days of your initial trip payment AND at least 31 days before departure, insuring all nonrefundable costs, with cancellation at least two days out — and New York modifies it to "cancel for any fortuitous reason"
No annual/multi-trip plan appears on the plans page (as of 2026-07-18), so frequent travelers need a competitor
State variation is real and specific — for example, a published $50 deductible applies if your primary residence is in Connecticut, Indiana, Kansas, Missouri, Montana, Vermont, or Washington
best_for: Travelers on trips under $10,000 who want the longest published change-your-mind window and a simply structured three-tier choice.
summary: Travelex's documented strengths are simplicity and the group's longest free look at 21 days, with 75% CFAR available on its Ultimate tier. The trade-offs: CFAR's stack of conditions is the most restrictive here, there's no annual plan, and several states carry a published deductible.
verdict_summary: Travelex ranks fifth in this comparison, but its published terms will suit a specific traveler well. Its 21-day free look is the longest change-your-mind window any provider here documents — a full refund if you're not satisfied, haven't departed, and haven't claimed, per travelexinsurance.com as of 2026-07-18. The lineup is refreshingly simple (Essential, Advantage, Ultimate, plus travel-medical and flight-only plans), the underwriter is a single named company (Zurich American, NAIC #16535), and the state-by-state notes are unusually specific. The honest trade-offs: Cancel For Any Reason lives only on the Ultimate tier and stacks conditions — 75% reimbursement capped at $7,500, trips of $10,000 or less, purchase within 21 days of first payment and at least 31 days before departure, cancel two days out, modified in New York; there is no annual plan; and seven states carry a published $50 deductible. This rating reflects published documentation, not claims experience.

faq.question: What is Travelex's free-look period?
faq.answer: Travelex publishes a 21-day free look — the longest in our comparison: if within 21 days of purchase you're not satisfied with your plan and haven't departed or filed a claim, Travelex refunds the plan cost (as of 2026-07-18).

faq.question: What are the conditions on Travelex's Cancel For Any Reason?
faq.answer: CFAR is available only on the Ultimate plan and reimburses up to 75% of prepaid, nonrefundable insured trip costs to a $7,500 maximum. New York residents get a modified "cancel for any fortuitous reason" version (as of 2026-07-18).

faq.question: Does Travelex offer an annual plan?
faq.answer: As of 2026-07-18, no annual or multi-trip plan appears on Travelex's official plans page — the lineup is six single-trip plans. Frequent travelers who want annual coverage should compare Allianz's AllTrips, Travel Guard's Annual plan, Seven Corners' Annual Multi-Trip, or World Nomads' Annual Multi Trip.

evidence_points.claim: Travelex's CFAR upgrade is available on Ultimate only: up to 75% of insured trip cost (max $7,500), trip cost ≤ $10,000, purchase within 21 days of initial trip payment and at least 31 days before departure, cancel at least two days before departure; modified for NY residents (as of 2026-07-18).

name: Travelpro Platinum Elite 21″ Expandable Carry-On Spinner
price_summary: $390 US list price (per travelpro.com as of 2026-07-18); softside expandable spinner, 46 L, 7.8 lb.
pros: The strongest published protection terms in this comparison after Briggs & Riley: a "Built for a Lifetime Limited Worry Free Warranty" on wheels, zippers, and handles, PLUS the Trusted Companion Promise, which pays warranty-repair shipping and covers "damage caused by an airline or other common carrier" (as of 2026-07-18)
A 100 Day Trial with a full refund if the bag "fails to meet your expectations for any reason" — and Travelpro pays return shipping, the most generous documented trial here
Largest published capacity in this ranking at 46 L (with 2 in. of expansion), while still listing a 21 x 14 x 9 in. case size
Unusually complete published spec sheet: external USB-A and USB-C ports, MagnaTrac® self-aligning spinner wheels, PrecisionGlide® system, and a fold-out suiter are all documented on the product page
cons: The exterior dimension including wheels and handles is 23 x 14.5 x 9 in. — bigger than the published 22 x 14 x 9 in. limit at American, Delta, and United — so the fit depends on the 21 x 14 x 9 in. case measurement; a stuffed, expanded bag may face gate scrutiny
At 7.8 lb it is the heaviest bag in this comparison — nearly a pound heavier than the Away or Monos hardsides

At $390 list it costs $115 more than the Away or Monos while being softside, and the warranty's blanket coverage applies to specific components (wheels, zippers, extension and carrying handles) rather than the whole shell
best_for: Frequent flyers who want maximum documented capacity and the most generous published trial-and-warranty package short of a $695 buy-it-for-life bag.
summary: Travelpro's Platinum Elite 21″ pairs the group's biggest published capacity (46 L, expandable) with its most generous documented trial (100 days, any reason, return shipping paid) and airline-damage coverage via the Trusted Companion Promise. It is also the heaviest bag here and its with-wheels dimensions exceed the big-three airlines' published limits.
verdict_summary: The Travelpro Platinum Elite 21″ Expandable Carry-On Spinner is our top overall pick on published terms. Its documented protection package leads its price class: a lifetime limited warranty on wheels, zippers, and handles, a Trusted Companion Promise that pays repair shipping and covers airline-caused damage, and a 100 Day Trial refunding the $390 list price for any reason with return shipping paid, per travelpro.com as of 2026-07-18. Its published 46 L capacity with 2 in. expansion is the largest here, and the spec sheet — USB-A/USB-C ports, MagnaTrac® wheels, fold-out suiter — is unusually complete. The honest trade-offs: 7.8 lb makes it the heaviest in this ranking; the 23 x 14.5 x 9 in. exterior (with wheels) exceeds the 22 x 14 x 9 in. limit published by American, Delta, and United, so fit rests on the 21 x 14 x 9 in. case size; and $390 is a real premium over the hardside competition. This rating analyzes published documentation, not lab testing.

faq.question: Will the Platinum Elite 21″ fit as a carry-on?
faq.answer: Travelpro publishes two sizes: a 21 x 14 x 9 in. case dimension and a 23 x 14.5 x 9 in. exterior including wheels and handles (as of 2026-07-18). American, Delta, and United all publish a 22 x 14 x 9 in. carry-on limit, so the with-wheels measurement technically exceeds it — in practice sizing depends on the airline's sizer and how full the bag is. Avoid flying with it expanded if you're worried about gate checks.

faq.question: What does Travelpro's warranty actually cover?
faq.answer: Two layers, per the product page: the "Built for a Lifetime Limited Worry Free Warranty" covers wheels, zippers, extension handles, and carrying handles, and the Trusted Companion Promise adds paid warranty-repair shipping and coverage for damage caused by an airline or other common carrier (as of 2026-07-18). It is a limited warranty on named components, not an unconditional whole-bag guarantee.

faq.answer: Yes — Travelpro publishes a 100 Day Trial: a full refund if the bag fails to meet your expectations for any reason, with return shipping paid (as of 2026-07-18). That is the most generous documented trial in our comparison.

name: Briggs & Riley Baseline Essential Carry-On Expandable Spinner
price_summary: $695 US list price (per briggs-riley.com as of 2026-07-18); hardside expandable spinner, 41–51 L, 8.6 lb.
pros: The only unconditional lifetime guarantee in this comparison: Briggs & Riley's "Simple as that®" guarantee states that "if your bag is ever damaged—even by an airline—we'll repair it, for life. Free of charge, no proof of purchase needed" (as of 2026-07-18)
CX® expansion is the largest documented range here — 41 L compressing back from up to 51 L ("up to 25% more space, then compresses back to carry-on size")
Published build details other brands don't match: 3-layer polycarbonate shell, YKK® self-repairing zippers, aerospace-grade aluminum handle, built-in TSA lock, and a PowerPocket™ for USB charging
Complete, precise published specs — 22 x 14 x 9 in. (expanding to 11.25 in. deep), 8.6 lb, 41–51 L — make airline-fit judgment easy
cons: $695 list price is 2.5x the Away or Monos and $305 more than the Travelpro — a serious premium that only pays off over many years of use
8.6 lb is the heaviest bag in this ranking, a real cost against airlines with cabin weight limits and for anyone lifting it into overhead bins
Flying it expanded (up to 11.25 in. deep) exceeds every major US airline's published 9 in. depth limit, so the extra space is realistically for the trip home or checked segments
best_for: Buy-it-for-life travelers who will trade a $695 price and extra weight for the only repair-anything-forever guarantee in the category, airline damage included.
summary: The Baseline Essential's documented case rests on its "Simple as that®" guarantee — lifetime repairs, airline damage included, no proof of purchase — plus the largest expansion range (41–51 L) and the most detailed build documentation here. The price is the con: $695 and 8.6 lb make it the most expensive and heaviest bag in this ranking.
verdict_summary: The Briggs & Riley Baseline Essential Carry-On Expandable Spinner ranks second overall and first on protection terms. Its "Simple as that®" guarantee is the only unconditional one in this comparison: lifetime repairs of any damage — explicitly including airline damage — free of charge with no proof of purchase, per briggs-riley.com as of 2026-07-18. The documented hardware backs it up: a 3-layer polycarbonate shell, YKK® self-repairing zippers, CX® compression-expansion from 41 L up to 51 L, a TSA lock, and a PowerPocket™ for USB charging, in a published 22 x 14 x 9 in. footprint. The honest trade-offs decide the ranking: $695 list is two-and-a-half times the hardside competition, 8.6 lb is the heaviest here, and using the full 11.25 in. expanded depth exceeds every major US airline's published carry-on limit. This rating analyzes published documentation, not durability testing. If you amortize luggage over decades, this is the documented pick.

faq.question: What makes the Briggs & Riley warranty different?
faq.answer: Most luggage warranties are limited — they cover manufacturing defects on named components and exclude airline damage. Briggs & Riley's published "Simple as that®" guarantee is unconditional: if the bag is ever damaged, even by an airline, they repair it for life, free, with no proof of purchase (as of 2026-07-18). In this comparison only Travelpro's separate Trusted Companion Promise also covers airline damage.

faq.question: Is it worth $695?
faq.answer: That depends on your time horizon. Against a $275 Away or Monos, the premium buys the unconditional lifetime repair guarantee, the 41–51 L expansion range, and documented hardware like YKK self-repairing zippers. Amortized over decades of travel it can be rational; for occasional trips, the cheaper bags' published terms are strong enough that the premium is hard to justify. That is why it ranks second here despite the best protection terms.

faq.question: Can I fly with it expanded?
faq.answer: Cautiously, no. Expanded, the published depth reaches 11.25 in., which exceeds the 9 in. depth in the 22 x 14 x 9 in. carry-on limit published by American, Delta, and United. The CX® system is designed to compress back to the 9 in. carry-on profile — treat the expansion as packing headroom for hotels and the trip home, not extra flying capacity.

name: Away The Carry-On
price_summary: $275 US list price (per awaytravel.com as of 2026-07-18); hardside polycarbonate spinner, 41 L, 7.5 lb.
pros: Strong documented value: a 100% polycarbonate shell, patented double-buckle compression system, TSA-approved combination lock, interior organization, and an included water-resistant laundry bag at a $275 list price (as of 2026-07-18)

The clearest published lifetime program in the mid-price tier: Away LifetimeCare™ includes complimentary repairs for five years, one replacement in that period if a repair isn't possible, and continued repair support with prepaid shipping afterward
100-day free returns and exchanges on unused items — matching Monos and rivaling Travelpro's trial window
At 21.7 x 14.4 x 9 in. including wheels and 41 L, its published exterior stays closer to the big-three airlines' 22 x 14 x 9 in. limit than the Travelpro's with-wheels measurement
cons: The published exterior — 21.7 x 14.4 x 9 in. — is still 0.4 in. over the big three's published 14 in. width, a nominal overage worth knowing about even if sizers rarely catch it

LifetimeCare™'s complimentary window is five years, after which repairs continue but are no longer stated as complimentary — extending full coverage to 10 years and two replacements requires paying for LifetimeCare™ Pro
The 100-day return window applies to unused items only, so it is a change-of-mind window, not a real-world trial like Travelpro's use-it-and-return-it 100 Day Trial
best_for: Travelers who want a documented, well-rounded hardside at a mid price with a clear published repair program and no obvious weak spot.
summary: Away's The Carry-On is the balanced pick: verified 41 L / 7.5 lb polycarbonate hardware with compression and a TSA lock at $275, backed by the published LifetimeCare™ program and 100-day unused returns. Its published protections are each a notch below the best in class — complimentary repairs cap at five years, and the trial excludes used bags.
verdict_summary: Away's The Carry-On ranks third as the strongest all-rounder per dollar. Its published package at $275 — 100% polycarbonate shell, 41 L capacity at 7.5 lb, patented compression, TSA-approved lock, and an included laundry bag — has no documented weak spot, and its 21.7 x 14.4 x 9 in. exterior including wheels sits closest to the major airlines' published 22 x 14 x 9 in. limit of the expandable-free bags here, per awaytravel.com as of 2026-07-18. LifetimeCare™ is the clearest mid-tier protection program in this ranking: five years of complimentary repairs, a replacement if a repair fails, then lifetime repair support with prepaid shipping. The honest trade-offs: the complimentary window is five years (10 years and two replacements costs extra via LifetimeCare™ Pro), the 100-day returns cover unused bags only, and the width nominally exceeds the big three's 14 in. by 0.4 in. This rating analyzes published documentation, not drop testing.

faq.question: What does Away LifetimeCare™ actually promise?
faq.answer: Per the product page (as of 2026-07-18): complimentary repairs for the first five years, one replacement within that period if the bag can't be repaired, and continued repair support with prepaid shipping for the life of the suitcase after year five. An optional paid LifetimeCare™ Pro extends complimentary repairs to 10 years with up to two replacements. It is a repair program with a five-year complimentary window — not an unconditional forever-free guarantee like Briggs & Riley's.

faq.question: Can I try The Carry-On and return it?
faq.answer: Away publishes free returns and exchanges within 100 days — but on unused items only (as of 2026-07-18). You can evaluate it at home, but once it has flown it is yours; Travelpro is the only brand in this comparison whose published trial refunds a used bag.

faq.question: Will it fit airline sizers?
faq.answer: Away publishes 21.7 x 14.4 x 9 in. including wheels. American, Delta, and United publish 22 x 14 x 9 in. limits, so The Carry-On is nominally 0.4 in. over on width while under on height and at depth. It is marketed as sized for major-airline overhead bins; if your itinerary involves strict regional or international sizers, check the specific airline's published limits.

Lifetime warranty is included with every purchase, plus a 100-day trial, per monos.com (as of 2026-07-18)
Aerospace-grade, water-resistant polycarbonate shell made from partially recycled materials at the same $275 list price as the Away
cons: Monos's key specifications — dimensions, weight, capacity, materials — are not published on the product page itself; we had to verify them from the brand's separate size-comparison pages, which is a real transparency gap when you're comparing bags

The published warranty is a headline ("Lifetime Warranty included with every purchase") without the detailed what's-covered wording that Briggs & Riley, Travelpro, and Away publish alongside theirs — read the fine print before you rely on it
At 39.9 L it has the smallest verified capacity in this ranking, 1.1 L under the Away at the same price and 6.1 L under the Travelpro
best_for: Weight-conscious packers who want the lightest verified hardside here, in exactly airline-limit dimensions, at a mid price.
summary: The Monos Carry-On is the lightest bag in this comparison (7.01 lb) with a published footprint that exactly matches the big-three airlines' 22 x 14 x 9 in. limit, backed by a lifetime warranty and 100-day trial at $275. Its documentation is the weak point: key specs live off the product page and the warranty's published terms are thin.
verdict_summary: The Monos Carry-On ranks fourth but wins two specific contests: verified weight and airline fit. At a published 7.01 lb it is the lightest bag in this comparison, and its 22 x 14 x 9 in. exterior is the only one that matches American, Delta, and United's published carry-on limit exactly — no nominal overages, per monos.com as of 2026-07-18. The aerospace-grade polycarbonate shell, included lifetime warranty, 100-day trial, and $275 list price make the value case against the identically priced Away. The honest trade-offs are documentary: Monos does not publish dimensions, weight, or capacity on the product page itself (we verified them via the brand's comparison pages), the lifetime warranty's published wording lacks the component-by-component detail its rivals provide, and 39.9 L is the smallest verified capacity here. This rating analyzes published documentation, not durability testing. For gram-counters and strict sizers, it is the pick.

faq.question: How big and heavy is the Monos Carry-On really?

faq.question: What are the terms of the Monos trial and warranty?
faq.answer: Monos advertises a lifetime warranty included with every purchase and a 100-day trial; the trial applies to unused items in brand-new condition with original packaging (as of 2026-07-18). The warranty's published headline doesn't detail component coverage the way Travelpro's or Briggs & Riley's do, so review the full warranty terms before relying on specifics.

faq.question: Monos or Away at the same $275?
faq.answer: On published documentation: choose Monos for the lower verified weight (7.01 vs 7.5 lb) and exact 22 x 14 x 9 in. airline-limit fit; choose Away for more verified capacity (41 vs 39.9 L), a more precisely documented repair program (LifetimeCare™'s five-year complimentary window and replacement terms), and fuller on-page specs. Neither publishes a used-bag return option — Travelpro is alone in that.
